items.issue: By the remainder theorem, p(a)=0 makes x−a both a divisor and a factor. Each is a printed option in both editions.
items.resolution: Show both valid terms and identify the key’s choice. An official erratum could remove the equivalent distractor.

steps.ta: p(a) = 0 எனில் (x − a) ஒரு காரணி; விருப்பம் (4).
steps.eq: By Factor Theorem, p(a) = 0 ⇒ (x − a) is a factor

items.issue: The printed stem does not specify the leading coefficient. All answer choices have a=1. Tamil calls the expression ஈருறுப்புக் கோவை, though the expanded quadratic has three nonzero terms.
items.resolution: Derive the general quadratic as a nonzero multiple of the product, then select the only listed choice that matches.

items.issue: The chapter defines a constant polynomial by degree zero and treats the zero polynomial separately.
items.resolution: State the nonzero-constant rule and the zero-polynomial exception explicitly in both languages.
items.proof: c=c·x⁰ for c≠0. For c=0 no exponent has a nonzero coefficient.

steps.en: Option (4) is correct (note: zero polynomial 0 has undefined degree).
steps.eq: A nonzero constant c = c·x⁰ has degree 0

items.issue: Neither source says the primes are distinct. Repeating the same prime gives that prime as the GCD, including the other listed value 2.
items.resolution: Teach both cases without a single graded choice. An official erratum could specify that the primes must be distinct.
items.proof: gcd(p,q)=1 for p≠q prime. gcd(p,p)=p, so gcd(2,2)=2.

steps.eq: Distinct primes share only 1 (and equal primes are not meant here; standard TN answer is 1)
